steps.why: Files live in kernel memory; test/fixtures/fs-growth.c grows one by appending or by setting its size, in MiB.

steps.script: ./fs-growth append under 2047 && test $(stat -c %s under) = 2146435072 && rm under
./fs-growth size sized 3072 && test $(stat -c %s sized) = 3221225472 && rm sized

steps.why: A growth past what memory can hold fails with ENOSPC (51, Dolly's errno), and the kernel and the shell carry on.
Appending needs no second copy of the file: it filled most of 8 GiB.
steps.script: test $(stat -c %s full) -gt 6442450944 && rm full && ./fs-growth append under 2047 && rm under
